solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drives straight into entrance of coastal town

parts.note: to ram something is to drive straight into it; 'drives' is the third-person form
a gate is a way in to a field or yard

explanation.surface: Directions for a motorist told to drive straight through the way in to a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: RAMSGATE is a seaside town on the Kent coast of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramsgate is an example: a port and resort on the Kent coast.

clue.text: Stays in auction (which could go either way) hosted by communists

indicators.note: hosted by puts the two-way letters inside the word for communists

parts.note: Reds is the old nickname for communists
bi, short for bisexual, describes someone who could go either way

explanation.surface: Communists run an auction where a bid might swing in either direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A bidder who offers again stays in the auction, so the verb for bidding again fits.

clue.text: Wise men's vice which Aladdin once had control of

definitions.text: which Aladdin once had control of

parts.note: the Magi are the wise men of the Nativity story
a clamp is a vice, a tool that grips work tightly

explanation.surface: The wise men have a weakness that once held Aladdin in its grip.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale, Aladdin owns the lamp that summons a genie at a rub.

clue.text: Hens urge caterer to mix drink

indicators.note: to mix tells the caterer to blend these letters together into something new

explanation.surface: Hen-party guests press the caterer to make cocktails.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a French herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks, so a drink.

clue.text: No-one standing in support on top of dais which has a rug

indicators.note: on sits the earlier pieces above the next letter in this down entry
in places nought and up inside the golfing support

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
O is zero, nobody at all
standing means up, on one's feet

indicators.note: top of takes the first letter of dais

explanation.surface: Nobody stands on the podium, which is carpeted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rug' is slang for a hairpiece, so a head that wears one is described.
explanation.definitionFit: A rug is slang for a wig, so a head with one wears a hairpiece.

clue.text: Money order for Roderick?

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a money order is meant for a man named Roderick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money order' looks like one financial phrase but splits into two pieces. Roderick Random is the hero of Tobias Smollett's 1748 novel, so the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist Smollett named his picaresque hero Roderick Random, so this is the surname that follows that first name.

clue.text: Perhaps Kylie Minogue is Queen of Football

parts.note: the pop singer Kylie Minogue was born in Melbourne
a queen rules her realm

explanation.surface: A claim that the pop star Kylie Minogue reigns over football.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of the code of football played on oval fields, mainly in Australia.

clue.text: Director of international body has power to come up and search me

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is the international body

indicators.note: to come up in a down entry means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a machine with power is on

explanation.surface: The UN chief has authority to come and search a speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'search me' is not a request for a frisk but a shrug: I have no idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal ways of saying I have no idea, a shrugging reply.

clue.text: Not on target about university failing to follow the instructions

indicators.note: about means the word for off target goes round the letter for university

parts.note: a shot that is not on target is missing

explanation.surface: Off-target students at a university ignore what they are told.
explanation.definitionFit: Using a device wrongly, against its directions, is exactly what not following instructions means.

clue.text: Searches larks

definitions.meaning: pats down a person for concealed items
plays or gambols about friskily, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both patting down a suspect and skipping about playfully.

clue.text: Make a dreadful mistake losing new horn

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter drops out of the longer word for the mistake

parts.note: to bungle is to botch something badly

explanation.surface: A musician makes a terrible blunder and loses a brand-new instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugle is a simple brass instrument of the horn family, used for military calls.

clue.text: America goes round forcing open rebellions

indicators.note: goes round says the two letters for America surround the word for levering open

parts.note: prising is levering something open with force

explanation.surface: A news line: America is circling the globe breaking open revolts.
explanation.definitionFit: Uprisings are revolts against authority, the same thing as rebellions.

clue.text: Alcohol containers heartless nobleman moves easily

indicators.note: heartless means the inner letters of the nobleman's title are removed, leaving its ends

parts.note: a duke is the highest rank of nobleman
a horse that canters moves at an easy pace between trot and gallop

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted aristocrat strolls through life with his drinks cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: Decanters are glass vessels into which wine or spirits are poured for serving.

clue.text: Automatons get rid of second- class carrots?

indicators.note: get rid of says a letter is thrown out of the word for the machines

parts.note: robots are automatons, machines that act on their own
B denotes second class, as in a B-grade

explanation.surface: Machines are told to throw out inferior carrots.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrots are an example of root vegetables, hence the question mark for definition by example.

clue.text: Remains asleep, presumably, if criticised

indicators.note: presumably signals that sleeping implies being in bed, so the remains go inside it

parts.note: someone asleep is presumably in bed
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Someone stays asleep, as you would if you had been savaged by critics.
explanation.walkthrough: The remains, ASH, are 'asleep', i.e. in BED.
explanation.definitionFit: To bash someone, informally, is to attack them verbally, so bashed and criticised are synonyms.

clue.text: Crusader's opponent wanting cold meal hot

parts.note: a salad is a meal served cold
something hot is fashionable, or in

explanation.surface: An enemy of the Crusaders is without a cold dish and wants a hot one.
explanation.walkthrough: Saladin was the twelfth-century sultan who fought Richard the Lionheart in the Third Crusade.
explanation.definitionFit: Saladin led the Muslim armies against the Crusaders and retook Jerusalem in 1187.

clue.text: One cutting into dead detective's area

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, so a detective's gives DI'S
a sector is an area or zone

explanation.surface: Someone takes a slice of a detective's patch, now deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissector is someone who cuts open bodies to study them, such as a corpse in anatomy.

clue.text: Know-it-all spoils race after you and I take first and second

indicators.note: after puts the jumbled race behind the earlier pieces
take says the pair for us holds the letters for first and second inside

parts.note: you and I together are we
I is one, the first

indicators.note: spoils means the word race is damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: A smart alec ruins a race after we finish first and second.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is someone who pretends to wisdom, a smart alec or know-all.

clue.text: One drinks after beginning to make trades

indicators.note: after puts the drinks behind the first letter of make

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the opening letter of the word make

parts.note: ports are fortified wines from Portugal

explanation.surface: A merchant has a drink after starting to do business.
explanation.definitionFit: Imports, as a noun, are goods brought in from abroad, a sense of trades or merchandise dealt in.

clue.text: Rotting this way in record time? Contrariwise!

indicators.note: Contrariwise flips the stated containment, so the record and time go inside this way rather than the reverse

parts.note: sic, Latin for thus, means written this way
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Something decays this way within a record time, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken at face value the clue puts 'this way' inside 'record time'; 'Contrariwise!' tells you the container and its contents swap roles.
explanation.definitionFit: Septic means infected and putrefying, so decaying or rotting.

clue.text: Ice has melted piece of furniture

indicators.note: ice that has melted has lost its shape, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Ice has thawed on a sofa or seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaise is a long reclining chair, as in chaise longue, so a type of furniture.

clue.text: Pass over German wearing a perfume

indicators.note: over puts the pass above the rest in this down entry

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: wearing means the single word for a surrounds the letter for German

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: Someone goes over a mountain pass, a German wearing scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de Cologne is a light scented water, named after the German city.

clue.text: Fourth military aircraft was pretty uninteresting

parts.note: a drone is an unmanned military aircraft
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: The fourth military aircraft was rather dull.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak in a monotonous, dull tone is to bore listeners, being tedious.

clue.text: Last part of register contains article number

indicators.note: contains says the end of register holds the article within it
Last part of takes the closing pair of letters from the word register

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: The end of a register includes an item with a figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but something that numbs: ether was an early anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether was used as an anaesthetic, which deadens feeling, so it is a numbing agent.

clue.text: Ha'aretz's first comment piece expressed optimism

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the newspaper's name

parts.note: an op-ed is an opinion column printed opposite the editorial page

explanation.surface: The Israeli newspaper Ha'aretz's lead opinion column sounded hopeful.
explanation.definitionFit: To have wished for an outcome confidently is to have shown optimism.

clue.text: White hunter giving two identical hats to Dr Spooner

indicators.note: Dr Spooner, the Oxford don, swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words are exchanged at the start

parts.note: a bowler is a round hard felt hat
a pair is two matching things

explanation.surface: Someone gives Dr Spooner two matching hats for a safari hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: BOWLER PAIR, with its first sounds swapped, says the answer; 'White hunter' is an Arctic predator.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar bear is a white-coated predator that hunts seals on Arctic ice.

clue.text: Accurately describing international mathematician

parts.note: a player picked for their country wins a cap, so an international is a cap
Alan Turing was the British mathematician and codebreaker

explanation.surface: A description of an international mathematician that is spot on.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch a likeness or a mood exactly is to get it precisely, describing it accurately.

clue.text: Admit what passengers hope a bus conductor will do to them

definitions.text: what passengers hope a bus conductor will do to them
definitions.meaning: waiting passengers hope the conductor allows them to board

explanation.surface: Passengers at a stop hope the conductor lets them board.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean allowing someone in, literally onto a bus or figuratively into a secret.

clue.text: Caribbean vegetable delicacy suffices after starters of eel and duck

indicators.note: after puts the word for suffices behind those opening letters
starters of picks the opening letters of eel and duck

parts.note: does means is enough, as in that will do

explanation.surface: A Caribbean dish is enough after first courses of eel and duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddoes are taro-like tubers eaten throughout the Caribbean and West Africa.

clue.text: Determined setter, guaranteed to lose, succeeded

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

indicators.note: to lose says one letter must drop out of the word for guaranteed

parts.note: assured means guaranteed, certain
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A resolute setter, sure to fail, came out on top anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: A measured response is deliberate and considered, so measured can mean determined or resolute in manner.
